topic: When will your money double? The rule of 72 (and how it works on prices too)
caption:
When will your money double? One number does the maths: 72.

Divide 72 by the yearly rate and you get roughly how many years it takes to double. Illustrative rates, not a promise of any return:
4% a year: about 18 years.
6% a year: about 12 years.
8% a year: about 9 years.
12% a year: about 6 years.

It works on prices too. If inflation runs at 6% a year (an illustrative figure), costs double in about 12 years. ₹50,000 of monthly expenses today could need about ₹1 lakh then. Money that grows slower than prices is quietly shrinking.

It's a rough shortcut, closest for rates between about 4% and 12%. Real returns move around and can be negative in some years.

Save this. Send it to someone whose savings sit idle.

Sources: published explainers on the rule of 72 (72 ÷ rate = years to double). Inflation and rupee figures are our illustrative calculations.
For education only. Not investment advice.
